content_voiceover: This slide is a high yield summary of every FDA approved indication for blinatumomab, the CD19 by CD3 bispecific T cell engager, and it's worth memorizing this list verbatim for boards. First, adult B-ALL relapse, established by the TOWER trial published in the New England Journal in twenty seventeen. Second, pediatric B-ALL relapse, based on a twenty sixteen Journal of Clinical Oncology study. Third, and this is a big bucket, B-ALL with positive MRD as a bridge to allogeneic stem cell transplant, supported by three separate trials, the phase two BLAST trial in Blood twenty eighteen, the AALL1331 trial for younger patients aged one to thirty one with relapsed B-cell ALL, and the twenty one twenty zero two one five trial for pediatric patients with high risk B-precursor ALL in first relapse, published in JAMA twenty twenty one. Finally, the newest indication, B-ALL with negative MRD used as consolidation therapy, based on a twenty twenty four New England Journal publication. So the four indication categories to remember are relapsed disease in adults, relapsed disease in children, MRD positive bridging to transplant, and now MRD negative consolidation, which represents blinatumomab moving earlier into frontline consolidation therapy.
keypoints: Adult B-ALL relapse: TOWER trial, NEJM 2017
MRD-positive bridging to allo-HSCT: BLAST, AALL1331, trial 20120215
keypoint_voiceover: Four FDA indications for blinatumomab to memorize: relapsed B-ALL in adults from the TOWER trial, relapsed B-ALL in children, MRD positive disease bridging to transplant across three supporting trials, and the newest one, MRD negative consolidation from the twenty twenty four New England Journal publication.
